documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
63 y/o man transferring care; his last doctor retired and a neighbor recommended the membership model.

Lungs: told he had emphysema in 2014 (age 56) after years of breathlessness on hills. Followed by a pulmonologist at his old office, who put him on tiotropium and, after an overnight oximetry study, oxygen at 2 L by cannula while he sleeps. Uses albuterol a couple of times a week, mostly carrying groceries up his porch steps. Says breathing is 'about where it's been.' No recent flares or prednisone bursts that he can recall.

Urinary: slow stream and gets up 2x a night; on tamsulosin at bedtime for years, happy with it.

Other: takes acetaminophen now and then for aches. Smoked about a pack a day for 40 years, quit spring 2019 cold turkey. Beer with friends maybe once or twice a week. Worked 30 yrs as a mechanic at the shipyard and then metal fabrication shops; retired 2018. Divorced, lives alone, drives.

PSH: appendectomy at 34, right knee scope at 52.
Family: father lung cancer at 72 (deceased), mother type 2 diabetes and pancreatic cancer at 78, brother prostate cancer at 68, paternal grandfather bladder cancer.
Allergies: sulfa (rash), shellfish.

Exam: Comfortable at rest, speaks full sentences. Lungs with mildly diminished air movement, no wheeze, no crackles. Heart regular, no murmur. Abdomen soft, healed RLQ scar. No clubbing, no edema. Gait normal.

A/P
1. COPD/emphysema: continue tiotropium daily, albuterol prn, overnight O2 2 L. Requesting old PFTs and pulmonary notes.
2. BPH with LUTS: continue tamsulosin.
3. Tobacco use disorder, sustained remission: congratulated.
4. Health maintenance: CMP, CBC, lipids, A1c today; one-time hep C and HIV screen. Flu shot given. Will ask old office for colonoscopy report.
RTC 6 months, sooner prn. Request records from prior primary care office.

documents.title: Immunization
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Quadrivalent flu vaccine given IM left deltoid. VIS provided. Tolerated without issue.

documents.title: Your recent lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Michael, your blood work looks good. Kidney and liver tests normal, blood counts normal, sugar (A1c) normal at 5.6, LDL cholesterol 104. Hepatitis C and HIV screens negative. Nothing to change. Talk soon.

events.reason: Records from prior primary care office

documents.title: Prior Primary Care Records Summary
documents.author: front desk
documents.body:
Records received by fax from patient's previous internal medicine office (42 pages), scanned under Media.

Contents: office notes 2012-2020; pulmonary clinic notes 2014-2019 documenting emphysema and starting tiotropium; overnight oximetry 2019 with recommendation for nocturnal oxygen 2 L/min; colonoscopy report 2018, normal exam to the cecum, no polyps, ten-year interval suggested; immunization record.

Flagged for PCP review.

documents.title: Outside Records Review
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Reviewed old chart. Consistent with his account: emphysema since 2014 on tiotropium; overnight O2 since 2019. Colonoscopy 2018 clean, next due 2028. Updated health maintenance.

documents.title: DME Recertification
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Home oxygen company called; they need a signed order and face-to-face note from the new PCP to continue his overnight concentrator. Sent new-patient note and order for O2 2 L/min via nasal cannula during sleep. PCP signed.

documents.title: Got both shots
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Finally got both covid shots at the clinic at the senior center, Jan 28 and Feb 18. Pfizer. Card attached. Arm ached one night, that was all.

documents.title: RE: Got both shots
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Thank you! Both doses are entered in your chart now.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Here for routine follow-up. Winter was quiet. Breathing unchanged, albuterol a few times a week. Wears O2 at night, machine working. Up twice to urinate at night as before.

O: Vitals reviewed. Lungs diminished but clear. Heart RRR. No edema.

A/P: COPD with emphysema stable on tiotropium. BPH stable on tamsulosin. Refills sent. Wellness visit in the fall.

documents.title: Refill Request
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Electronic request for tiotropium capsules and tamsulosin 90-day supply. Last visit March, stable. Approved x 4 refills each.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Initial Medicare AWV.

Functional: independent in all ADLs and IADLs, drives, does his own shopping and cooking. No falls in the past year. Hearing ok in quiet rooms, a bit of trouble in restaurants (years of shipyard noise). Vision fine with readers.
Cognition: three-word recall 3/3, clock drawing normal.
Mood: PHQ-2 0.
Safety: smoke detectors, no firearms, wears seatbelt.
Advance directive: none; given blank health care proxy form, he will think about who to name.

Exam: lungs diminished, clear. Heart RRR. No edema.

Prevention: flu today. Discussed pneumococcal (PCV20) and shingles series; he'll come back for a nurse visit next month with his COVID booster. Colonoscopy 2018 normal. Hep C/HIV done 2020.
Personalized plan printed and reviewed.

documents.title: Immunization
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Influenza quadrivalent 0.5 mL IM right deltoid. No immediate reaction.

documents.title: Nurse Visit — Immunizations
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Here for vaccines per PCP plan. Screening questions negative. Given: PCV20 left deltoid; Pfizer COVID booster right deltoid; Shingrix dose 1 left deltoid (separate site, 1 inch apart). Observed 15 min, no reaction. Reminded second Shingrix due in 2-6 months, booked for January.
